purpose: Machine contract of the DarkPlanner Studio editorial library. GENERATED from code (core/enfases-meta, core/perfis-*, core/editorial-doc, core/contrato-v2, core/regras-tempo, core/predefs-edicao and the physical catalogue) — never edit by hand (npm run gerar:biblioteca). Read guidance, rules, presets and intake first; highlights/templates/catalogs are the universe. Hard rules (exclusive subtypes, denied subtypes, manualOnly, universe of the active preset, timing rules) are enforced by the application on intake — a proposal that breaks them is rejected with a reason, never silently fixed.

colorSystem.derivation: tonsDaPaleta(primaria) → claro/vivo/medio/escuro; a neutral colour (saturation < 28) is never replaced; aplicarPaleta dresses the accent fields (corDado/decorCor/tagCor/…)

languages.detection: The document language is detected from the speech text itself (pt/en/es packs) and drives the local engine signals: dates, chapters, counts, fractions, impact words, connectives. Other languages (fr, de, it…) fall back to the pt pack for signals; years, %, currency symbols and bible references (generic net) still work. Fonts cover latin + latin-ext; non-latin scripts render in the system font.
languages.rule: Every text field follows the language of the speech — never translate the speech. Labels derived by the engine (LOCAL/ANO/DADO…) are editor defaults in Portuguese: the AI SHOULD rewrite them in the language of the video.

filling.rule: When a style is applied to a speech block, the main field comes from the speech; optional fields are derived (sequential index per style, century in Roman numerals on the era card, label by text type, value/label of a percentage, bible reference) or stay EMPTY — they never inherit the catalogue sample. The AI fills optional fields through each field aiInstruction BEFORE applying; empty is valid.
filling.authoredText: The AI may write its own text for a highlight (a thesis, a label, a shortened sentence) instead of the literal speech — it must relate to the passage, keep the language of the speech, respect the style word range and fit the time window (rules.text).

bible.detection: Reference = Book chapter[:verse[-end]] in any language. Full names and abbreviations in PT/EN/ES for the 66 books (numbered books accept 1/2/3, I/II/III, 1st, first, primeiro, primer…); separators : . , and a dash range; generic net for other languages (Capitalised name + ch:verse, e.g. "Jean 3:16", "Johannes 3:16"). Guards: short abbreviations (≤4 letters) only count WITH a verse; a book that is also a person name (John, Luke, Daniel…) needs a verse or a numeric prefix; clock times, years and "Chapter 3" are not references.
bible.normalisation: The reference is rewritten with the full book name in the active language: "Jn 3,16" → "João 3:16" (pt) / "John 3:16" (en) / "Juan 3:16" (es). In a language without a pack the abbreviation stays as written. Chapter only ("Psalm 23") becomes the form "capitulo".
examples: "I can do all things through Christ who strengthens me." — Philippians 4:13
For God so loved the world (John 3:16)
Porque de tal manera amó Dios al mundo — Juan 3,16
bible.fields: verse (text without the reference) · reference (normalised) · book/chapter/verses (derived) · version (only if cited).

guidance.readingOrder: biblioteca-indice.json first (compact universe, ~10k tokens); then this file only for the styles/templates you intend to use (by id); rules/presets/intake are the contract you must obey.

rules.golden: The SPEECH anchors the reading point. A highlight enters preRoll before the first spoken word of its block (the animation impact lands exactly when the word is said), covers the WHOLE speech of the block, and breathes a tail into the silence up to the next speech. ONE highlight on screen at a time — neighbours never overlap. This holds for the local engine, for manual application and for anything the AI proposes: the intake recomputes start/end from these rules and rejects what cannot fit.

timing.anchor: The speech anchor of a highlight is the first spoken word OF ITS OWN TEXT, never the start of the block group: literal text is located in the word JSON (its first 2-3 words in sequence); authored/summary text must carry palavra or palavraIdx; a proposal whose text cannot be anchored inside a speech span longer than 2.5 s is rejected (texto autoral sem ancora na fala). The item appears at most preRoll (<= 0.5 s by class) before that word and keeps the tail rule after the speech ends.

sources.wordJson: per-word timings [{palavra, iniS, fimS}] from the narration — first/last spoken word of the block = falaIniS/falaFimS; a word anchor (palavra | palavraIdx) moves the impact to that word
sources.srt: caption blocks {id, startS, durationS, text} — used when there is no word JSON (block edges = speech edges)
sources.block: the speech caption is the unit: one highlight per block; the AI addresses blocks by their caption id

timing.preRollS: min(style class preRollMaxS, free space before the speech (≤ 0.6s, minus 0.04s from the previous highlight), animation impact + 0.08s)
timing.postRollS: min(1s, 45% of the gap until the NEXT speech) — the rest of the gap is reserved for the next highlight's pre-roll
timing.fitsInTime: available = speech duration + min(preRollMaxS, free space) + min(1s, 45% of next gap) must be ≥ class.minTotalS / class.maxSpeedUp — otherwise the style is not eligible for that block

classesKeys.maxSpeedUp: how much the gesture may be accelerated

collisionPolicy: 1. trim the TAIL of the previous highlight down to (at most) the end of its own speech — the tail is decorative
2. eat the PRE-ROLL of this one (it enters later, never after its speech starts); the impact moves with it, the end stays
3. almost overlapping speeches: shift anyway if ≥ 0.8s of the block remains (better late than two on screen)
a highlight already on the timeline is FIXED: it is never trimmed — a new proposal over the same speech is rejected

text.reading: reading duration of a text = 0.9s + beats / 2.5 per second, clamped 1.6–6s (a beat = a content word; connectives of the detected language do not count)
text.maxBeatsInWindow: floor((min(6, max(1.6, windowS)) − 0.9) × 2.5) — a text with more beats than this (+1 tolerance) is rejected; shorten it
text.wordRange: the text must respect the style `palavras` [min, max]
text.typing: typing styles (forma digitacao) are eligible only between 6 and 30 characters per second of the window
text.authored: AI-authored text is allowed (thesis, label, shortened sentence) — it must relate to the block, keep the speech language and obey the rules above; the literal speech is the default
text.fields: optional fields follow each aiInstruction; empty is valid; never inherit catalogue samples

selection.rolePriority: abertura → secao → destaque → enfase → info → apoio (budget per role first, then style/beat/position/sound resolvers with a diversity window)

ratesKeys.gapMinS: min seconds between two of the same role

hard: exclusivo: only when the block carries one of the style subtypes
info styles with declared subtypes: only the matching subtype
strict universe: never outside the active preset kit

templates.avatarClass: Templates Avatar are separate from normal scene templates. Choose them deliberately after reading SRT/Word narration and scene context; they use one Avatar and the underlying main scene, never reinterpret normal template slots. The templatesAvatar preset axis defaults off for older presets.
templates.avatarOccupancy: New normal templates reject any scene containing Avatar; multi-scene candidates are rejected whole, never repacked. Distributed Avatar skips scenes with normal templates. Whole-avatar placement may cover pre-existing normal templates and preserves them. An Avatar layout replaces only another Avatar layout, not a normal template.
templates.textFields: Every fixed label in a template ("CAPÍTULO", "TÓPICO", "PERFIL"…) is a SLOT for script text, never content: pass `campos` to studio_aplicar_template with the text derived from the speech of that stretch (same language, same case, within maxChars). A template left with its factory label is a defect.
templates.speechLabel: A template whose field source is "speech" writes the spoken caption of the take itself and COVERS the standard caption in that stretch (the editor hides it automatically) — never add a duplicate caption.

rhythmKeys.teto: density ceiling (sum of intensities in the neighbourhood)

physics: effects with motion only on still images
transitions never cross a gap; a junction under a template only gets breathing transitions (int ≤ 1)
a template needs N contiguous free takes ≥ 1s each and never overlaps an existing composite
the filter is a GLOBAL identity: one per video
manual edits are preserved on regenerate (values that diverge from the last applied plan)

catalogs.exits: same ids and profiles as entrances (applied at the end of the scene)

profileKeys.precisaImagem: effect only valid on still images (Ken Burns family)
profileKeys.durAlvoS: natural duration of the gesture in seconds (clamped to 35% of the scene)

presets.concept: A preset (Portuguese: predefinição / "Direção") packs the editorial universe the user allows: rhythm, colour mode, filters, effects, transitions, entrances/exits, templates and the highlight kit, each with a frequency (pct) and per-item weights. Applying a preset builds a deterministic plan (seed) — same seed, same edit. The AI receives the ACTIVE preset as `state.direcao.snapshot` and must edit inside it.

filtros|efeitos|transicoes|entradas|said.pct: 0–100 = share of scenes (transitions: of junctions; templates: of regions; templatesAvatar: eligible Avatar/main-scene intersections) that receive the category

itens.som: transitions only: sound override (auto | nenhum | file)

destaques.estilos: highlight style ids allowed (the kit); EMPTY = the active kit of the project

schema.legenda: { captionStyle, capCustom } | null — caption style bundled with the preset

universo.predef: STRICT: only what the preset marks may be used — a speech block with no compatible style in the kit gets NO highlight (never falls back to the system); templates/transitions/effects only from the marked lists
universo.sistema: the whole automatic catalogue: every category without marked items receives the full catalogue (weight 1); the kit becomes every auto-eligible style; pct values still apply

cores.predef: apply the preset colour as the project palette (tone on tone on every adaptive style)
cores.projeto: keep the colour defined in the Project Identity (capEnfase.paleta)
cores.auto: no forced palette: each style keeps its own colours; the AI may choose a coherent palette and write it to capEnfase.paleta {ativa, primaria, secundaria, acento}

semantics.ritmo: multiplies every pct by RITMOS_PLANO.fator and sets the density ceiling and breathing gaps (rules.plan)
semantics.densidade: budget of highlights per role over the video duration (rules.selection.densityFactors)
semantics.pesos: item share = peso / sum(pesos); repetition penalties (same id, same family) apply within a recent window
semantics.validation: unknown ids are removed and reported on apply (validarPredef); manual-only templates never enter a plan; empty highlight kit = project kit
semantics.coverage: coberturaDoKit(kit) lists roles and info subtypes the kit cannot serve — in strict universe those sentences stay without highlight; the editor is warned and the AI should not propose them

highlights.function: aplicarEventosIA(propostas, { seed, estilosPermitidos, universoEstrito, substituirLote }) — state/use-enfases (bridge verb to be exposed by the MCP server)

proposal.blocoId: caption id of the speech block (required)
proposal.texto: optional authored text (default: the block speech). If it quotes the speech, its first 2-3 words are located in the word JSON and anchor the highlight; if it is a summary, palavra or palavraIdx is REQUIRED on spans longer than 2.5 s
proposal.campos: optional field values by field id (see highlights[id].texto.campos)
proposal.palavra: word of the block that anchors the highlight (the item appears at most preRoll before it is spoken) — required for authored/summary text
proposal.palavraIdx: optional 0-based index of the spoken word in the block

result.descartes: [{blocoId, estilo, motivo}] — every rejected proposal with its reason

rejectionReasons: bloco já recebeu destaque nesta proposta
estilo só-manual (fora do sorteio e da IA)
estilo exclusivo de <subtipos> sem esse sinal no bloco
texto fora do alcance do estilo (min–max palavras)
texto autoral sem âncora na fala: use palavras ditas no trecho ou informe palavra/palavraIdx
palavra "<x>" não é dita neste bloco
não cabe no tempo: N batidas em Ts (máx ≈ M) — encurte para ≤M palavras
guarantees: start/end recomputed by rules.timing (never trusted from the proposal)
anchor = first spoken word of the highlight own text (rules.timing.anchor): the item never appears seconds before its words; word-accurate when the word JSON exists, SRT edges otherwise
no overlap with existing highlights nor between proposals
same materialisation as the local engine: own track above the captions, linked SFX by the sound policy, derived fields + AI fields

plan.function: aplicarComSeed(predef, seed) — state/use-direcao: the AI may produce the SAME plan object as core/plano.montarPlano (cenas/juncoes/templates) and it goes through validarPlano before landing atomically

planObject.cenas: { sceneId: { effect, fxParams, animIn, animOut, animDurS, filter, filterStrength } }

validation: effect/anim/transition ids must exist in catalogs
no transition on the last scene
templates: automatic only, existing scenes, no overlap with composites nor between templates

intake.colour: to choose a coherent palette when cores.modo = auto, write capEnfase.paleta = { ativa: true, primaria, secundaria, acento } (derive secundaria/acento with tonsDaPaleta(primaria) semantics: light/mid tones of the primary)

tpl_avatar_circulo.timing: The Avatar interval coordinates the presentation. A selected or explicit window may span adjacent Avatar clips and main scenes; saved source keys remain explicit. A continuous layout keeps the presenter stable while only the main-scene slot follows scene transitions. A real gap is never filled. Shortening the layout reveals the normal Avatar at its continuing timestamp.
tpl_avatar_circulo.edit: studio_editar ajustar kind composto campos.avatarLayout merges lado, escala, x/y, fundo, cor, raio, margem, formato (original or 16:9), gradeCor, gradeIntensidade (0..1), gradeMovimento (boolean), entrada/saida (suave or nenhuma) and animDurS. Grid layouts always use 16:9 frames. Timing edits must stay within the bound Avatar sources and main-scene coverage.
whenToUse: Avatar in a compact circular frame over the scene; use when the speaker should remain visible without taking the whole screen
whenNotToUse: Do not use without an Avatar clip or when the scene needs an unobstructed full frame
